newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index ends down in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index ends down in dull trade.

text.p: Jakarta shares ended down in dull trade on Wednesday as falls in some blue-chips were coupled with local-led profit-taking in secondaries, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 2.81 points, or 0.49 percent, to close at 565.78 points after touching a low of 564.41 points. Losers led gainers 69 to 42, with 53 unchanged.

Brokers said the market was likely to continue being sluggish on Thursday as some foreigners were sidelined while others were net sellers. "It is unusual that foreigners are not buying back yet even though some heavyweights are already at bargain levels," said a broker for foreign firm.

Some brokers said the sluggish situation was due to general negative sentiment on Indonesia. They named the controversial national car programme, which has been taken to the World Trade organisation by Japan, and a series of rumours on a takeover of Astra International, the country's biggest car manufacturer.
"Psychologically it gives a negative impact on market sentiment," said one local broker.
Others said some investors were sidelined as they were awaiting third quarter results or because they felt the primary market was more attractive.
Blue-chips telecommunication firm Telkom, satellite operator Indosat, cigarette firm Sampoerna and cement firm Semen Gresik were among the targets of foreign selling, brokers said.
Brokers said the declines in the heavyweights had pressured market sentiment which was already weak since the opening.
Telkom fell 25 rupiah to 3,525 on a volume of 2.5 million shares on what brokers said was in line with a slight fall in New York overnight.
Sampoerna fell 2.09 percent to 18,750 rupiah on what brokers said was the result of its purchase of a stake in Astra.
Shipping firm Berlian Laju Tanker was actively traded with 3.9 million shares changing hands. It rose 75 rupiah to 3,450 on speculation of a possible stock split, brokers said.

Secondary packaging firm Berlina was actively traded with 3.8 million shares changing hands, rising 50 rupiah to 1,575 rupiah on market talk that it would be taken over by one conglomerate. The company declined to give any comment.
